1: use ruff_diagnostics::{Diagnostic, Edit, Fix, FixAvailability, Violation};
2: use ruff_macros::{derive_message_formats, ViolationMetadata};
3: use ruff_python_ast::{self as ast, Expr};
4: use ruff_python_trivia::{SimpleTokenKind, SimpleTokenizer};
5: use ruff_text_size::{Ranged, TextSize};
6: 
7: use crate::checkers::ast::Checker;
8: 
9: /// ## What it does
10: /// Checks for unnecessary dictionary unpacking operators (`**`).
11: ///
12: /// ## Why is this bad?
13: /// Unpacking a dictionary into another dictionary is redundant. The unpacking
14: /// operator can be removed, making the code more readable.
15: ///
16: /// ## Example
17: /// ```python
18: /// foo = {"A": 1, "B": 2}
19: /// bar = {**foo, **{"C": 3}}
20: /// ```
21: ///
22: /// Use instead:
23: /// ```python
24: /// foo = {"A": 1, "B": 2}
25: /// bar = {**foo, "C": 3}
26: /// ```
27: ///
28: /// ## References
29: /// - [Python documentation: Dictionary displays](https://docs.python.org/3/reference/expressions.html#dictionary-displays)
30: #[derive(ViolationMetadata)]
31: pub(crate) struct UnnecessarySpread;
32: 
33: impl Violation for UnnecessarySpread {
34:     const FIX_AVAILABILITY: FixAvailability = FixAvailability::Sometimes;
35: 
36:     #[derive_message_formats]
37:     fn message(&self) -> String {
38:         "Unnecessary spread `**`".to_string()
39:     }
40: 
41:     fn fix_title(&self) -> Option<String> {
42:         Some("Remove unnecessary dict".to_string())
43:     }
44: }
45: 
46: /// PIE800
47: pub(crate) fn unnecessary_spread(checker: &mut Checker, dict: &ast::ExprDict) {
48:     // The first "end" is the start of the dictionary, immediately following the open bracket.
49:     let mut prev_end = dict.start() + TextSize::from(1);
50:     for ast::DictItem { key, value } in dict {
51:         if key.is_none() {
52:             // We only care about when the key is None which indicates a spread `**`
53:             // inside a dict.
54:             if let Expr::Dict(inner) = value {
55:                 let mut diagnostic = Diagnostic::new(UnnecessarySpread, value.range());
56:                 if let Some(fix) = (SpreadEdit {
57:                     source: checker.locator().contents(),
58:                     prev_end,
59:                 })
60:                 .unnecessary_spread_fix(
61:                     inner.start(),
62:                     inner.end(),
63:                     inner.iter_values().last().map(Ranged::end),
64:                 ) {
65:                     diagnostic.set_fix(fix);
66:                 }
67:                 checker.diagnostics.push(diagnostic);
68:             }
69:         }
70:         prev_end = value.end();
71:     }
72: }
73: 
74: struct SpreadEdit<'a> {
75:     source: &'a str,
76:     prev_end: TextSize,
77: }
78: 
79: impl SpreadEdit<'_> {
80:     /// Generate a [`Fix`] to remove an unnecessary dictionary spread.
81:     fn unnecessary_spread_fix(
82:         &self,
83:         dict_start: TextSize,
84:         dict_end: TextSize,
85:         last_end: Option<TextSize>,
86:     ) -> Option<Fix> {
87:         let mut tokenizer = SimpleTokenizer::starts_at(self.prev_end, self.source);
88:         let doublestar = loop {
89:             if tokenizer.is_bogus() && tokenizer.rest().is_empty() {
90:                 return None;
91:             }
92:             let token = tokenizer.next()?;
93:             if token.kind() == SimpleTokenKind::DoubleStar {
94:                 if &tokenizer.source_text()[token.range()] != "**" {
95:                     continue;
96:                 }
97:                 if tokenizer.current_offset() > dict_start {
98:                     return None;
99:                 }
100:                 break token;
101:             }
102:             if tokenizer.current_offset() > dict_start {
103:                 return None;
104:             }
105:         };
106: 
107:         if let Some(last_end) = last_end {
108:             // Ex) `**{a: 1, b: 2}`
109:             let mut edits = vec![];
110:             let mut tokenizer = SimpleTokenizer::starts_at(last_end, self.source);
111:             loop {
112:                 if tokenizer.is_bogus() && tokenizer.rest().is_empty() {
113:                     break;
114:                 }
115:                 let Some(tok) = tokenizer.next() else {
116:                     break;
117:                 };
118:                 if tok.kind().is_trivia() {
119:                     continue;
120:                 }
121:                 match tok.kind() {
122:                     SimpleTokenKind::Comma => {
123:                         if &tokenizer.source_text()[tok.range()] == "," {
124:                             edits.push(Edit::range_deletion(tok.range()));
125:                         }
126:                     }
127:                     SimpleTokenKind::RBrace => {
128:                         if &tokenizer.source_text()[tok.range()] == "}" {
129:                             edits.push(Edit::range_deletion(tok.range()));
130:                             break;
131:                         }
132:                     }
133:                     _ => {}
134:                 }
135:             }
136:             Some(Fix::safe_edits(
137:                 // Delete the first `**{`
138:                 Edit::deletion(doublestar.start(), dict_start + TextSize::from(1)),
139:                 edits,
140:             ))
141:         } else {
142:             // Ex) `**{}`
143:             Some(Fix::safe_edit(Edit::deletion(doublestar.start(), dict_end)))
144:         }
145:     }
146: }
